description: Fix 1a: dynamic execution-provider (EP) auto-selection with probe-verified fallback, a single startup log line naming the engaged EP, and LAYA_EXECUTION_PROVIDERS as an explicit override that skips auto-selection. Runtime picks the best EP that ACTUALLY initializes a working session; a listed-but-broken EP (e.g. 'DirectML unsupported by this model') falls through to the next candidate and never crashes or dead-ends. This is the ONE fast/decision path; do not add several ways.
steps: DESIGN DATA SHAPES FIRST (architect). Add a small, mostly-pure resolver module `src/laya/execution-provider.ts`. Suggested shape (adjust names for clarity): `interface EpCandidate { name: string; providers: string[] }` where `name` is the human label for the log line ('cuda'|'directml'|'webgpu'|'cpu') and `providers` is the onnxruntime executionProviders list to pass to Laya.load (each GPU candidate should include a CPU fallback entry, e.g. cuda -> ['cuda','cpu']). A PURE function `candidateExecutionProviders(platform: NodeJS.Platform, arch: string, override?: string[]): EpCandidate[]` returns the ordered candidate list. When `override` is provided, return exactly one candidate wrapping it verbatim (auto-selection is skipped). Otherwise return the platform-appropriate preference order: prefer CUDA on linux x64, DirectML on win32 x64/arm64, WebGPU where applicable, and ALWAYS end with a plain CPU candidate so resolution can never fail. Base platform gating on the onnxruntime-node@1.30.0 prebuilt support facts recorded in the briefing (CPU everywhere; DirectML Windows x64/arm64; CUDA linux x64 CUDA v12; WebGPU experimental); do not offer a candidate the platform cannot host.

Design the IO probe boundary so the probe REUSES the real session creation rather than duplicating a warmup: because Laya.load throws when a listed EP cannot initialize the model, attempting LayaEngine.load with a candidate's providers IS the probe. Add an async resolver, e.g. `resolveEngine(candidates: EpCandidate[], load: (providers: string[]) => Promise<T>, log: (line: string) => void): Promise<{ engine: T; chosen: EpCandidate }>` that tries candidates in order, keeps the FIRST that loads without throwing, catches each failure and continues to the next, and returns the loaded handle (so the model is loaded ONCE, not probed-then-reloaded). If every candidate throws, rethrow the last error so createEngine's existing try/catch degrades to UnavailableEngine (never crash the server).

Wire it end to end WITHOUT breaking boundary discipline: src/config.ts already parses LAYA_EXECUTION_PROVIDERS into config.executionProviders (keep that). In src/laya/index.ts createEngine, when the real engine is to load, build the candidate list from config.executionProviders (as override) or auto-select via process.platform/process.arch, then use the resolver to load LayaEngine once and return it. Keep ONNX imports confined to src/laya/engine.ts; the resolver stays free of direct ort imports (it only orchestrates a load callback + pure candidate list).

Emit ONE startup log line naming the engaged EP. src/index.ts currently writes '[laya-browser-mcp] Autopilot engine loaded.' to stderr when engine.available. Extend that line (or add one adjacent line) to name the chosen EP, e.g. '[laya-browser-mcp] Autopilot engine loaded (execution provider: cuda).'. The chosen EP name must flow out of the resolver to this log point (e.g. expose it on the engine or return it through createEngine). Keep it to a SINGLE line and never on stdout (stdout is the JSON-RPC stream).

TDD the ORDERING and the FALL-THROUGH-ON-FAILURE with a FAKE session factory (no GPU here). Add `test/execution-provider.test.ts` (vitest): (a) candidateExecutionProviders returns CPU-last on every platform and the expected GPU-first order per platform/arch, and returns exactly the override candidate when an override is supplied; (b) resolveEngine tries candidates in order and returns the FIRST whose fake load resolves; (c) when the first candidate's fake load REJECTS (simulating 'DirectML unsupported by this model'), resolveEngine falls through and returns the next working candidate, and the chosen name reflects the fallback; (d) when ALL fake loads reject, resolveEngine rejects (so createEngine degrades). Assert the resolver loads the model exactly ONCE on the happy path (spy call count).

Keep the existing offline behavior intact: with no weights and no override, createEngine must still return UnavailableEngine (the resolver only runs on the real-engine path). Confirm test/config.test.ts LAYA_EXECUTION_PROVIDERS parsing still passes; extend it only if needed.
acceptance_criteria: candidateExecutionProviders is a pure function, always ends its list with a CPU candidate, honors an explicit override by returning exactly that single candidate (auto-selection skipped), and gates GPU candidates by platform/arch per the onnxruntime-node 1.30.0 support matrix.
resolveEngine loads the model once, keeps the first candidate that initializes, falls through to the next on a load failure, and rejects only when every candidate fails.
The server logs exactly one startup line naming the engaged EP (to stderr), and LAYA_EXECUTION_PROVIDERS still works as an explicit override that skips auto-selection.
New unit tests in test/execution-provider.test.ts cover ordering, override, fall-through-on-failure, all-fail, and load-once; they pass with a fake factory and require no GPU.
pnpm run typecheck clean, pnpm run build exit 0, pnpm test still green (baseline counts + the new tests).
The actual GPU speedup is labelled UNVERIFIED-here / to-be-measured on the user's RTX 4050 (documented in FEAT-006), not fabricated.
verification: bash -lc 'pnpm test' (new execution-provider tests pass; suite stays green)
